credit: Written for the app from the Calderwick city data, an original setting.

entries.title: Smoke fog
entries.text: When the smoke fog settles on Lowfield it can sit for days: the tube mills' chimneys vanish, the gas lamps burn at noon, and the pneumatic post is the only thing in town that keeps to time.

entries.title: Pennine rain
entries.text: Pennine rain comes in grey and steady: the setts shine in the Market Place, clogs clatter on the wet flags, and the canal boats on Saltergate Basin go under tarpaulins.

entries.title: Snow on the moor
entries.text: Snow on Ridley Moor closes the moor road, the airship mail stays tied to its mast, and the children of Hobcroft sledge down the ginnels.

entries.title: A warm day
entries.text: On a warm day the whole town goes up to Calder Holme: the lido, the velodrome, the pier on the old mill dam and ice-cream carts from Paradise.

entries.title: Spring
entries.text: In spring the curlews come back to the moor, washing dries outside again, and the light evenings bring the first brass band concert in Ackroyd Park.

entries.title: Wakes week
entries.text: In summer the smoke lifts, and in wakes week the mills shut, half the town takes the train to the seaside and the other half has the fair at Calder Holme.

entries.title: Autumn
entries.text: In autumn fires are lit again, the children go chumping for wood for their street's bonfire, and slabs of parkin are baked to be better a week later.

entries.title: Winter
entries.text: In winter it is dark by half past four, forced rhubarb comes pink from the dark sheds, and the worst smog of the year sits in the valley in December.

entries.title: Before the hooter
entries.text: Before the six o'clock hooter the knocker-up goes along the terraces tapping on bedroom windows with a long pole, and the streets fill with the clatter of clogs heading down to Lowfield.

entries.title: Saturday
entries.text: Saturday is payday and market day: stalls on the setts, tripe shops and pie-and-peas, the Sunday suit redeemed from Uncle's, and the Theatre Royal full at night.

entries.title: The pneumatic post
entries.text: Calderwick tubes its notes across town by pneumatic post: a quick answer is "back down the tube" and a lost one has "gone up the pipe".

entries.title: Lowfield
entries.text: Lowfield is chimneys in every direction, the tube mills' hiss and the foundries' glow; where there is muck, the town says, there is brass.

entries.title: Ridley Moor
entries.text: On Ridley Moor the wind never stops, the reservoirs shine, and the mail airship ties up at its mooring mast above the town.

entries.title: Bonfire Night
entries.text: On Bonfire Night every street lights the bonfire its children have guarded for weeks, there is parkin and treacle toffee, and the fire brigade spends the night on call.

entries.title: Whit Monday
entries.text: On Whit Monday the chapels and Sunday schools walk through the town behind their banners and brass bands, the children in new clothes, then have tea and races in a field.

entries.title: Christmas
entries.text: At Christmas the Co-op windows are dressed, carols ring out from the chapels, and the works shut for two whole days, which some still think an extravagance.

entries.title: At the works
entries.text: At the works the day runs from hooter to hooter: tea is mashed strong in a brown pot at break, and the mild ale flows at the pub by the gate after the shift.
